chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Know that whatever insects you trample, or which your camel tramples, upon you is its ransom.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing insects while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific liability for accidentally killing small land creatures (daba) while in the state of Ihram, distinguishing it from other forms of hunting. It highlights the scholarly consensus that mere trampling by a person or their mount incurs a fidah (ransom), reflecting the broader juristic principle of compensating for minor violations of sanctity during pilgrimage. The ruling underscores the meticulous attention to detail in Shia fiqh regarding the preservation of sacred spaces and states.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Know that whatever is trampled upon from the insects, or trampled by your camel, so upon you is its ransom’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You must take notice that whatever moving things you or your camel may step on, you owe ransom therefor.’”
